title: Existence of a minimum-weight spanning tree
statement: Let $G$ be a connected simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $w$ assign a real weight $w(e)$ to each unordered pair $e$ of vertices. Then there exists a spanning subgraph $T$ of $G$ that is a tree and whose total edge weight $\sum_{e \in E(T)} w(e)$ is least among all subgraphs $T'$ of $G$ that are trees.
hypotheses_covered: V is a finite vertex set
w is a real-valued weight on unordered pairs of vertices
T is a subgraph of G (T ≤ G)
T minimizes total edge weight over all subgraph-trees T' of G
